title: This is what 2 weeks of Opus 5.5 looks like
author: acem13
selftext:
It is not a one prompt game, it all started with a very small prototype then little by little I started adding things.

In first I defined that game should be in three.js, set the color pallet I wanted and gave Opus a design for characters. Then defined game rules and gameplay mechanics.

Then started building a bigger open world, added quests, more characters, story and overall always improved gameplay.

Game-trailer was also created in the same Opus 5.5 with direction from me.

Will keep working on game and release full game soon, you can check Steam page here - [Orange Braincell](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5375400/Orange_Braincell/)

replies.author: UnboundedMan
replies.body: Blocky models. Most of opus 5.5 game creators have them.

replies.author: acem13
replies.body: No it was all built only with three.js

comments.author: game_plaza
comments.body: Are you wrapping the web game into an executable to ship on steam e.g. electron, tauri?

replies.author: acem13
replies.body: With electron and Opus 5.5 does it itself so it was quite easy to first version up to Steam, but it had fps problem, took me 3 times to fix it properly by describing issues to Claude

replies.author: game_plaza
replies.body: Nice! Had thought about doing this. Glad to see its feasibility confirmed. I've read that tauri is more performant but have no experience with either. Though, electron probably has a larger community and is more mature. Interesting approach indeed!
